top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu offers the longest and most varied record in which to judge a sustained, whole-oeuvre project. Public descriptions suggest his large books change structure and narrating stance rather than restate one another, and the voice and formal ambition appear distinctive. Both points are unverified: I have not read the texts, and the density of the Romanian may be only partly carried by translation. The poetry is thinly covered in translation, so the citation should rest on the prose. The margin over Wright and Michon is narrow. It turns on breadth and duration against depth in fewer books. If a comparison of the volumes showed repetition, the preference would weaken, and no award would still rank below every named candidate.
